Iris: hey all, Iris herefirst day on platform. Following the quickstart but `kubectl get pods -n tools` gives `Error from server (Forbidden)`. Who handles kubeconfig / RBAC?
Noel (eng-infra): welcome Iris :wave: we do. Can you paste `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n tools`? Are you using SSO or a local kubeconfig?
Iris: current-context is `rwd-dev-us-west`, `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n tools` -> no. I'm on SSO (browser). Email iris@redwood.com.
access-bot: created INFRA-3344 for iris@redwood.com. Assigned: Noel. ETA ~20m.
Noel (eng-infra): quick workaround while we sync your groups: create a short-lived namespace-scoped serviceaccount. Run:```bash
kubectl -n tools create serviceaccount iris-onboard || true
TOKEN=$(kubectl -n tools create token iris-onboard --duration=6h)
kubectl config set-credentials iris-onboard --token="$TOKEN"
kubectl config set-context iris-tools --cluster=rwd-dev-cluster --namespace=tools --user=iris-onboard
kubectl config use-context iris-tools
```
Iris: running the token command now...
Iris: token created and switched context, `kubectl get pods -n tools` now works. thanks!! :tada:
Harper: fyi -- SA tokens are visible in audit logs. If you need elevated permissions for a demo request a timed elevation so it is tracked.
Noel (eng-infra): added a RoleBinding for `group:developers` in `tools` so after you reauth your SSO you'll keep access without the SA. Also, to avoid context mixups we recommend per-shell KUBECONFIG files (eg `~/.kube/iris/tools`) or our `kctx` helper that warns on prod contexts. DM me for the helper.
oncall-bot: note: oncall runbook for the tools namespace is at /docs/oncall/tools-k8s. Ping @oncall if you see service degradations.
Iris: confirmed after re-login SSO group shows developers and I can `kubectl` without the temp context. Really appreciate the fast help and the warm welcome :smile:
Noel (eng-infra): welcome aboard Iris! If anything else blocks you DM me or drop into #eng-infra.
